concerns.text: T013d flags trials with cue-reward delay <500ms but does not halt; T013g only halts if >50% are confounded. This silently relaxes Plan.md Phase 0 Step 2 which mandates a 'REJECT' or 'HALT' of the Neural Correlates claim if metadata is missing or invalid, creating a semantic weakening of the safety constraint.

T042a and T043a implement mandatory HALT/REJECT logic for missing time-resolved data or spike sorting metadata (Plan Phase 0 requirements) but are marked as unimplemented `[ ]` in the 'Polish' phase. This leaves core constitutional safety gates (Constitution Principle VI) unimplemented in the main pipeline flow.

T016b attempts to persist data loss metrics to `state/artifact_hashes.json`. This violates Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) which requires `state/` to store checksums, not raw metrics. This is a semantic drift of the artifact's purpose, risking data integrity tracking.

T004 (checksum generation) depends on T006 (schema) but not explicitly on T005 (synthetic data generation). If T004 runs before T005, the checksum file will be incomplete. This violates the deterministic execution order required for Constitution Principle III (Data Hygiene) and reproducibility.

T024 (MDES) depends on T022a (observed variance), but the task list order in Phase 4 places T022 (Dispersion) before T022a. Without an explicit dependency declaration or ordering, the pipeline may attempt MDES calculation before variance is computed, violating the logical constraint of the statistical workflow.
